issue_context.title: Split promql package into parser and engine
issue_context.body:
## Motivation

Currently the `promql` package includes both the PromQL parser and the PromQL engine.

The PromQL language server imports this package, but actually only needs the parser part.

Importing the full PromQL package, brings a several disadvantages, compared to only importing the parser:

* A lot of unnecessary dependencies are included. This makes the language server binary almost three times larger, than it would be when only importing the parser part.
* The engine transitively depends on several operating system specifics, such as mmap or unix system calls. This makes it impossible to compile the language server for certain platforms, like Web Assembly.

## Proposal

It is proposed to create a new `parser` subpackage in the `promql` package that only includes the parser.


cc @brian-brazil @juliusv @roidelapluie
comments: I'm for it, I know at least one other use case already where people have made a fork and removed engine bits for this reason (https://github.com/influxdata/promql).
I agree with this too. It makes sense.

review_comments: I don't think this belongs to the parser

Not really.

However, `testStmt` is of type `Statement`, which can only be implemented in the parser package because of https://github.com/slrtbtfs/prometheus/blob/split_parser/promql/parser/ast.go#L54 .


The alternative to what I'm doing would be making `Statement.stmt()` public, so `testStmt` could live in the engine, but that kind of defeats the point of  `Statement.stmt()`.

Since having one more `Statement` type in the parser doesn't really hurt I decided to go that way.
Having the list of functions in two places feels wrong.

The reason for that is that the implementation of the function calls shouldn't belong to the parser package, but the type information should.

Do you have an idea for another way to achieve this?
Not offhand, but at the least we should have a test that the two have the same elements.
